prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1368; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Officers responded to a reported two-vehicle collision in Katy, Texas, involving a low-speed head-on impact. Driver 1 was operating a sedan westbound when it struck the front of a sport utility vehicle operated by Driver 2. Driver 1 stated that the impact caused a wrist injury and was unable to say at the scene whether the symptoms were new or related to an earlier condition. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of the sedan and confirmed being in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Responding officers observed front-end damage to both vehicles that is consistent with the reported impact, and scene photographs document the same areas of contact. No independent witnesses were located, and no statements from bystanders were obtained. Officers found no indication of prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as a household member of the policyholder, who resides at the same address, and was identified as an authorized operator of the sedan. Further medical review will be needed before any link between the reported wrist injury and this collision can be determined.
